text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
NASA BORBA
- Around 75 percent of health and social workers in major Serbian towns on general strike since Monday over late wages, only emergency services operating.
- Montenegrin parliament to convene for first session since rift in leadership of the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro.
- Yugoslav and Belgian foreign ministers discuss possibility for extending international presence in Eastern Slavonia region in Croatia.

- Bosnia-Herzegovina's survival depends on how fast its communities will accept the fact that people of different religions and customs can live together, says Deputy High Representative for Bosnia Robert Farrand.
- Croatian, Serb representatives agree to hold first session of Vukovar-Srem district on May 24.
- Healthy banking system is the Yugoslav central bank's priority, says National Bank of Yugoslavia Deputy Governor Ratko Banovic.
- Serbian government's proposal for separating postal services from telecommunications most complicated and risky, Nasa Borba says in commentary.
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav foreign minister's visit to Belgium, the first to a European Union member-country since the EU granted Yugoslavia trade preferentials in late April, is important for overall bilateral relations, Belgium plans significant investments in Yugoslavia, says Belgian foreign Minister.
- Agreements on pensions and health insurance payments with Croatia and Macedonia expected to be reached in June, says Yugoslav labour ministry.

- Federal parliament agriculture committee proposes draft law on transforming farm debt into public debt. Debts in primary agricultural production reached two billion dinars ($35.7 million) late last year.
- Works on 12-kilometer section of Kocani-Pecenjevce highway in southern Serbia, towards Macedonia, to resume, completion expected by July 31.
- Yugoslavia plans major investments in modernisation of its heating and electric power plants, says Yugoslav economy minister Rade Filipovic.
- Djerdap I hydro-electric power plant produced 8.3 million kwh of electricity last year, or 25 percent above plan.
- Growing interest among foreigners in Yugoslav banks, says Association of Yugoslav banks.
- MONTENETGRO -
POBJEDA
- Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) local branch of Pljevlja unanimously proposed to the party's main board DPS president Momir Bulatovic as presidential candidate for the next elections.
- "DPS as a ruling party has a right to create state policy, from concrete moves to appointments," says Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic in TV Montenegro interview.
- The government of Montenegro passed its opinions on draft laws to Montenegrin parliament which convenes today.
- Delegation of trade chamber of Bari (Puglia, Italy) on a visit to Montenegro. Italian businessmen interested in purchase of timber, building material and aluminium.

- Electrolux of Sweden and Montenegrin health ministry sign contract in Podgorica Wednesday worth 1.2 million German marks for refurbishing kitchen facilities of Podgorica Central Hospital. The contract is part of a 20 million mark deal for refurbishment of Montenegrin health institutions signed at the start of the year. Electrolux to open its office in Podgorica.
- Executive board of TV Montenegro adopted guideline on media presentation of parliamentary political parties. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 43045
